olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Integers at vertices of regular pentagon sum to 2011. A turn: subtract $m$ from two adjacent vertices, add $2m$ to the opposite vertex. Won at a vertex if that vertex reaches 2011 and others reach 0. Prove there is exactly one winning vertex for any initial assignment.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2011

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Nonconvex, non-self-intersecting hexagon $ABCDEF$: $\angle A=3\angle D$, $\angle C=3\angle F$, $\angle E=3\angle B$; $AB=DE$, $BC=EF$, $CD=FA$. Prove $AD,BE,CF$ are concurrent.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2011

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: For $n\geq 2$, does $2^{2^n}\bmod(2^n-1)$ always give a power of 4? Prove or find a counterexample.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2011

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $P$ inside $ABCD$. $Q_1,Q_2$ inside with $\angle Q_1BC=\angle ABP$, $\angle Q_1CB=\angle DCP$, $\angle Q_2AD=\angle BAP$, $\angle Q_2DA=\angle CDP$. Prove $Q_1Q_2\parallel AB\Leftrightarrow Q_1Q_2\parallel CD$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2011

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $|A|=225$; $A_1,\ldots,A_{11}\subseteq A$ with $|A_i|=45$ and $|A_i\cap A_j|=9$ for $i\neq j$. Prove $|A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_{11}|\geq 165$ and give an example of equality.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2011
